digest.top_line: PRIMARY2: PSMA-PET triage of PI-RADS 2-3 MRI cut csPCa detection 12% vs 16% (diff -3·7%, p=0·0093 NI) and avoided biopsy in 49%.
digest.tldr: Prostate carried the day, and it is a diagnostic-pathway result, not a treatment one: PSMA-PET as a pre-biopsy triage step in equivocal MRI held non-inferior csPCa detection while halving biopsies and cutting insignificant-cancer overdiagnosis 32% → 14%. Fewer, better-selected men reaching definitive RT is the downstream consequence; 6·0-month median f/u and differential missing biopsy data cap confidence.

sites.intro: First randomised test of PSMA-PET as a pre-biopsy triage tool, upstream of any RT decision but shaping who arrives at one.

studies.name: PRIMARY2
studies.tldr: csPCa 12% vs 16% (diff -3·7%, 95% CI -8·9 to 1·5; p=0·0093 non-inferiority) with PSMA-PET triage; biopsy avoided in 49%.
details: 🔍 Phase 3 non-inferiority RCT, 1:1, N=660, seven Australian hospitals, unmasked, stratified by site
🔍 Biopsy-naive men, PI-RADS 2 or 3 MRI plus ≥1 clinical red flag (PSA density >0·1, family hx, abnormal DRE, BRCA, PSA >10, PSADT <36mo, PSA velocity >0·75/yr), PSA ≤20, ≤cT2
📊 Co-primary 1: csPCa (Gleason 3+4 with ≥10% pattern 4 or higher) 39/331 (12%) experimental vs 51/329 (16%) control; difference -3·7% (95% CI -8·9 to 1·5), p=0·0093 against a 10% margin
📊 Co-primary 2: PSMA-PET avoided biopsy in 163/331 (49%, 95% CI 44 to 55), p<0·0001 vs the 20% threshold
📊 Clinically insignificant cancer 105/329 (32%) control vs 46/331 (14%) experimental, difference -18% (97·5% CI -25 to -11), p<0·0001

details.text: 📊 Alternate csPCa definitions and sensitivity analyses (ITT unless stated)

details: 📐 PRIMARY score negative (1-2) in 166 (50%) of 329 scanned; positive (3-5) in 163 (50%); central vs local reader κ=0·81 (95% CI 0·75-0·87)
📐 Cores per biopsied participant 24·8 (SD 9·0) control vs 19·6 (12·1) experimental; no biopsy in 35 (11%) control vs 173 (52%) experimental

⚠️ Biopsy data missing differentially: 35 (11%) control vs 7 (2%) experimental did not get protocol biopsy, and the worst-case analysis crosses the 10% margin once four of those 35 control men truly harbour csPCa
⚠️ Median follow-up only 6·0 months (IQR 5·1-7·0); the 159 unbiopsied PSMA-negative men have PSA surveillance, not a histological reference standard
⚠️ No masking of participants or investigators, and control-arm PI-RADS 3 men could add MRI-targeted cores, so biopsy technique differed by arm beyond the imaging question
🔗 Only prior data were the non-randomised PRIMARY (2021) NPV study; this is the first randomised test of PSMA-PET as a pre-biopsy triage tool

verdict.rationale: Randomised phase 3, co-primary endpoints met, prespecified margin. Divergence from MRI-only pathway is real, though unmasked with 6-month follow-up and differential missing biopsies.
verdict.audience: Biopsy-naive men, PI-RADS 2-3 MRI with a clinical red flag, PSA ≤20, ≤cT2

studies.significance: The number that gates transferability is the PET threshold, not the HR: PRIMARY score 1-2 sent men to PSA surveillance, and SUVmax ran 3·9 (IQR 3·3-4·6) in negatives vs 5·2 (4·3-7·1) in positives, with κ=0·81 between central and local readers. For a radiation oncologist this changes who arrives in clinic, halving insignificant Gleason 6 referrals (32% to 14%) without losing csPCa.
studies.monday_clinic: In a biopsy-naive man with PI-RADS 2-3 MRI, PSA ≤20 and a clinical red flag, this supports PSMA-PET as a triage step before transperineal biopsy; it does not speak to men with PI-RADS 4-5 MRI, prior biopsy, or known prostate cancer.

primary_endpoint.name: Clinically significant prostate cancer (Gleason ≥3+4 with ≥10% pattern 4)

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Investigator-initiated **phase 3, multicentre, non-inferiority RCT** at seven Australian hospitals, 1:1 randomisation via REDCap with block sizes of two or four, stratified by site. **No masking** of participants or investigators. Enrolment March 2, 2022 to Aug 24, 2025; data cutoff Dec 5, 2025; **median follow-up 6·0 months** (IQR 5·1-7·0).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: 808 assessed, 148 excluded (124 declined, 22 ineligible), **660 randomised**. Biopsy-naive men with **PI-RADS 2 or 3** MRI plus at least one red flag (PSA density >0·1 ng/mL/mL, abnormal DRE, strong family history, BRCA, PSA >10, PSA doubling time <36 months, or PSA velocity >0·75 ng/mL per year), PSA ≤20 ng/mL, clinical T2 or less. Median age 61 (IQR 56-66), median PSA 5·2 ng/mL, median PSA density 0·13; PI-RADS 2 in 335 (51%), PI-RADS 3 in 325 (49%). Ethnicity not collected.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Experimental arm: pelvic-only **[68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET-CT within 28 days** of randomisation, 1·8-2·2 MBq/kg (median administered 164 MBq, IQR 149-182), oral or IV furosemide 20 mg recommended, acquisition 60-70 min post-injection (median uptake time 61 min), low-dose CT without contrast, two bed steps from the iliac crests down. Whole-body PET was recommended when intraprostatic SUVmax reached 12 or more, or for seminal vesicle, nodal or distant uptake, and was done in 35 (11%). Scored centrally and locally, masked to MRI, on the five-point PRIMARY score with a second central reviewer as tiebreaker.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Co-primary:** proportion with clinically significant prostate cancer (Gleason 3+4 with ≥10% pattern 4 or higher on transperineal biopsy within 3 months), non-inferiority margin **10%**; and proportion in the PET arm avoiding biopsy within 6 months, against a **20% threshold**. Secondary: clinically insignificant cancer, alternate csPCa definitions, core number, interobserver variability, and biopsy complications by PRECISION and SHIM questionnaires.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Both co-primary endpoints met. **PRIMARY score positive (3-5) in 163 (50%)** of 329 scanned participants and negative (1-2) in 166 (50%), with score 1 in 30 (9%) and score 2 in 136 (41%); reader agreement κ=0·81 (95% CI 0·75-0·87). No cancer on biopsy fell from 138 (42%) of 329 to 73 (22%) of 331.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Among biopsied participants, post-biopsy symptom rates were similar: **pain 33 (21%) experimental vs 62 (21%) control**, haematuria 60 (38%) vs 126 (43%), haematospermia 77 (48%) vs 133 (45%). Erectile dysfunction on SHIM was unchanged from baseline in both arms (50 [31%] of 160 vs 91 [31%] of 294 after biopsy). The safety gain is structural, not pharmacological: 173 (52%) of the experimental arm had no biopsy at all.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The only prior evidence was the **non-randomised PRIMARY (2021)** study, which reported improved negative predictive value for csPCa in an MRI-triaged population going to systematic transperineal biopsy. The authors' own search found **no randomised trials** of [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET-CT in the diagnostic setting, so this is the first randomised read on PSMA-PET as a pre-biopsy triage step rather than a staging tool.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents biopsy-naive men with equivocal (PI-RADS 3) or non-suspicious (PI-RADS 2) MRI, at least one clinical red flag, PSA 20 ng/mL or less, and clinical T2 disease or less. Does not represent men with PI-RADS 4-5 MRI, prior biopsy or known prostate cancer, PSA above 20, or those already staged for definitive therapy.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Protocol biopsy data were **missing differentially**: 35 (11%) control vs 7 (2%) experimental. The prespecified worst-case scenario crosses the 10% margin once **four of the 35 unbiopsied control men** truly had csPCa, so non-inferiority rests on a thin assumption about missing histology. The 159 PSMA-negative men who skipped biopsy have PSA surveillance rather than a reference standard, and at 6 months only 51 (8%) have had prostatectomy and seven (1%) radiotherapy, so the durability of a negative PET is untested.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The trial reframes PSMA-PET from a staging tool into a **diagnostic triage** step, and its practical yield is as much about overdiagnosis as detection: insignificant cancer fell from 32% to 14% and mean cores per biopsied man from 24·8 to 19·6. Health-economic analysis and validation with other PSMA radiopharmaceuticals are named by the authors as the gaps before implementation.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The referral stream changes upstream of RT: insignificant Gleason 6 diagnoses fell from 105 (32%) of 329 to 46 (14%) of 331 with csPCa detection preserved (12% vs 16%). Fewer low-grade men enter surveillance or treatment discussions, though at 6 months only seven (1%) participants had received radiotherapy, so downstream treatment patterns are unreported.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Half the men (163 of 331, 49%) avoided transperineal biopsy entirely, and among those biopsied mean cores fell from 24·8 (SD 9·0) to 19·6 (12·1) because sampling was PET-targeted rather than systematic. The urological decision this moves is whether a PI-RADS 2-3 man with a red flag goes to the biopsy list at all.

open_questions: Durability of a negative PSMA-PET beyond 6 months of PSA surveillance

papers.title: Effect of [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET-CT in the diagnosis of prostate cancer in men with equivocal or clinically high-risk non-suspicious findings on multiparametric MRI (PRIMARY2): a multicentre, non-inferiority, phase 3, randomised controlled trial
